headline: Three back-to-back ultra days are logged and the trail block is complete. The engine held its shape at controlled HR throughout. The story now is absorption — recovery and the return to normal rhythm.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days
confidence_attention: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The three consecutive long days on foot dominate everything this week, and they close the crossing on the terms this block was built for: very long time on feet at deliberately capped HR, the third day sitting lower still than the first two. That last point matters — the athlete didn't blow up across three days, they held or even softened intensity, which is exactly the durability signal you want out of back-to-back ultra work. Strength has been absent through the crossing window, which is expected rather than concerning given what the legs were doing, though its return will be the honest marker that the block has been absorbed. Steps remain very high and essentially flat between rest and training days, so background load never really drops. Sleep has been short and fragmented through the crossing, and the cardio-load status still reads detraining — a rolling-average artefact of the taper that preceded these days, not a real reflection of what just happened. Recovery, not fresh load, is the job this week.
sections.trends: The medium-term shape is a clear, deliberate build: recent four weeks well up on the prior block, and year-to-date distance sitting at more than four times last year at this point. That surge is almost entirely the crossing, which is the intended peak of a long ramp rather than a runaway trend — expect the next few weeks to consolidate hard as the volume unwinds. Nothing here suggests overreach in the structural sense; it makes sense as the top of a planned arc, and the question is simply how cleanly the descent from it is managed.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and the VO2-adjacent markers are stale — the last threshold reading predates the crossing by weeks, and nothing in the recent log tests that end of the range. That's fine: three ultra-slow days tell you nothing about top-end fitness and shouldn't. The banked threshold work from earlier in the year is still the reference point, and it won't have eroded from a durability block. The real read on aerobic sharpness will come from the first genuinely paced session after recovery, not from anything in this window.
sections.zones: The distribution this week is almost entirely Z1, which is precisely correct for what these sessions were — controlled, sustainable time on feet where the whole point is staying off the gas. The per-session shapes confirm the discipline: even across the longest day, HR barely lifted out of the bottom zone, and the third day was the most restrained of the three. There's no grey-zone creep and no accidental drift into Z3 during long efforts, which is the classic failure mode of ultra-distance days. Intensity distribution matched intent cleanly. When speed work re-enters, that's when the zone picture should broaden again.
sections.hr_comparison: Nothing concerning in the strength HR history — the recent functional sessions sit low and steady, consistent with the earlier block. Across the crossing runs the HR held remarkably flat relative to the distances covered, which is the durability quality showing up in the data rather than any sensor question. No source-agreement issues worth flagging.
sections.calendar: The running streak is intact and the crossing sits inside it as a dense cluster of consecutive days — a genuine departure from the usual roughly four-times-weekly cadence. That clustering is the event, not a new baseline. What to notice over the coming days is the shape of the gap that follows: a sensible easing-off is expected and healthy, and the return of spacing between sessions is part of absorbing what was just done, not a break in consistency.
sections.personal_bests: None of the current bests are in play from this block — they live at the speed end, and nothing here touched that. The 50K best in particular is tied to an effort in the same family as this crossing, so if anything the durability just banked strengthens the base those long-distance marks sit on. Short-course PBs will only become relevant again once paced work resumes and the legs are fresh.

watch_items: Watch whether the cardio-load status flips out of detraining as the rolling averages catch up to the crossing — a slow flip would suggest the real cost ran higher than the low HR implied.
Watch the first easy runs back for elevated HR at normal pace, which would show the effort is still being paid down.
Watch when strength re-enters the log — its return marks that the trail block has been absorbed and normal rhythm resumed.
Watch whether sleep consolidates now that the crossing window has closed, since recent nights have been short and broken.
